objective: Build a paper-targeted Step 5 expansion queue focused on defensible positive evidence: direct-identity anchor neighborhoods, LR/L2-stable high-scoring discoveries, and identifier-control high-score candidates. Step 11 is used only as a candidate miner, not as ground truth.

robust_lr_l2_high_score_unreviewed.review_instruction: Review as possible non-identifier positive only if there is exact low-frequency text/structure closure strong enough to survive the template-resale objection. Do not mark positive from model score alone.

identifier_control_high_score_unreviewed.review_instruction: Use the identifier-augmented scorer only as a triage signal. Mark positive only with seller-facing shared contact or unusually strong content closure; product/victim-data emails and public URLs are not positives.

direct_proof_anchor_neighbor_unreviewed.review_instruction: This row touches a seller from a strict direct Telegram proof pair. It may reveal expansion around a known controller, but it is not independent proof and must not be placed in test without component-leakage review.

hard_rules: Never treat a Step 11 cluster as ground truth.
Never auto-promote a row to positive from model probability alone.
Product/victim-data emails, public content URLs, file-host links, and external URLs without seller-operated context are not direct identity positives.
Rows touching a proof-anchor seller must be handled as same-component risk; if later marked positive, split assignment must preserve seller/component isolation.
If this queue cannot find new direct-contact positives, report direct-identity evidence scarcity instead of diluting labels with weak positives.
